lessonActivities.title: Each & Every Basics – Individual vs Complete! 🎯
lessonActivities.content:
Welcome to the precise world of each and every! These determiners help us talk about individuals versus complete groups. 📚

Core Concept: Each emphasizes individuality ('one by one'), every emphasizes completeness ('all members').

Key Points:

Information
Each: Focuses on individual members one at a time
Every: Refers to all members of a complete group
Both: Used with singular nouns and require singular verbs

Important Note: Each can be used with just two items, but every needs three or more.

Common Mistakes: Using every when you mean each, or vice versa.
examples: Each employee received an invitation. (one by one)
Every pupil must wear a uniform. (all pupils)
He carried a book in each hand. (just two hands)
Every book borrowed must be returned. (all books)
Each refugee received food and water. (individual focus)
There is a train every 15 minutes. (regular complete schedule)
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Quick Test: Each = one by one. Every = all together.

lessonActivities.title: Each in Detail – Individual Focus 🚀
lessonActivities.content:
Master the specific uses of each for emphasizing individual treatment. 📈

Each Characteristics:

Information
Two or more items: Can be used with just two
Pronoun form: Each can stand alone as a pronoun
Distribution: Emphasizes separate treatment

Context Matters: Use each when you want to stress individual consideration.

Practice Strategy: Think of dividing things among individuals.
examples: A letter was sent to each of the firemen. (individual letters)
The prize money was divided among the team members. Each received 10,000€. (individual amounts)
Each of us has a computer. (every individual person)
Both girls work. Each earns a good salary. (separate salaries)
A meal was served to each of the passengers. (individual service)
He shook hands with each of his supporters. (individual handshakes)

lessonActivities.title: Every in Detail – Complete Group Focus 🔍
lessonActivities.content:
Learn the specific uses of every for referring to complete groups. 🎭

Every Characteristics:

Information
Three or more: Needs a complete group
Regularity: Used for frequency (every day, every hour)
Abstract nouns: Every reason, every possibility
With adverbs: Almost/practically every, nearly every

Regional Variations: Some dialects use every with smaller numbers informally.

Advanced Tip: Every implies no exceptions in the group.
examples: Every employee received a free copy. (complete group)
The church bells ring every hour. (regular complete cycle)
They have every reason to be satisfied. (all reasons)
A news bulletin is published every morning. (complete regular schedule)
We have every confidence in you. (complete confidence)
Nearly every student passed the test. (almost all students)
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Complete Focus: Every = the whole group without exception.

lessonActivities.title: Each vs Every – Critical Differences ⚖️
lessonActivities.content:
Master the crucial distinctions between each and every in context. ⚖️

Key Differences:

Information
Quantity: Each (2+), Every (3+)
Emphasis: Each (individual), Every (group)
Following words: Each + of, Every + noun directly
Implication: Each (separate), Every (inclusive)

Emotional Impact: Each sounds more precise, every more general.

Replace one with the other and see if meaning changes.
examples: Each child got a present. (individual presents)
Every child got a present. (all children included)
Each of the players was interviewed. (separate interviews)
Every player was interviewed. (complete team coverage)
She visited each city separately. (one by one)
The train stops at every station. (all stations on route)
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Meaning Test: Each = individual treatment. Every = group inclusion.

lessonActivities.title: Each/Every + One – Special Constructions 📊
lessonActivities.content:
Learn the special constructions with each one and every one. 📊

Special Forms:

Information
Each one: Each + one (emphasizes individuality)
Every one: Every + one (refers to all individuals)
With pronouns: Each/every one of us/them

Context Matters: Each one is more emphatic than each alone.

Use these forms for emphasis in formal writing.
examples: I would like to thank each one of you. (every individual)
The boss explained to every one of the employees. (all employees)
Each one of her ideas is worth considering. (individual ideas)
Every one of the copies must be registered. (all copies)
I have seven grandchildren. Each one is dear to me. (individual affection)
Every one of us has a responsibility. (all have responsibility)
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Emphasis Rule: Each one = stronger individual focus than each.

lessonActivities.title: Mastering Each & Every – Natural Usage 🏆
lessonActivities.content:
Put it all together! Use each and every naturally in real communication. 🏆

Communication Strategies:

Information
Individual treatment: Use each/each one
Regular events: Use every + time expression
Emphasis: Each and every together for stress

Advanced Tip: 'Each and every' is used for emphasis but means the same as 'every'.
examples: The manager explained to each and every one of you. (emphasized completeness)
Each participant received a certificate. (individual certificates)
The alarm rings every five minutes. (regular complete cycle)
I interviewed each one of the candidates personally. (individual interviews)
Every citizen has the right to vote. (complete group right)
She checked each item on the list. (one by one checking)
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Native Choice: Every is more common in speech; each sounds more formal.

writingActivities.question: Write 5 sentences using 'each' to emphasize individual treatment.
writingActivities.hint: Use each with of, or as a pronoun, focus on separate/individual actions.

writingActivities.question: Write 5 sentences using 'every' to refer to complete groups.
writingActivities.hint: Use every with complete groups of 3+, or for regularity/frequency.

writingActivities.question: Write sentences contrasting 'each' vs 'every' in similar situations.
writingActivities.hint: Show how they create different emphases in similar contexts.

writingActivities.question: Write sentences using 'each one' and 'every one' correctly.
writingActivities.hint: Each one emphasizes individuality, every one refers to all individuals.

writingActivities.question: Write sentences using 'every' with time expressions.
writingActivities.hint: Use every with words like day, week, hour, morning, etc.

writingActivities.question: Write a short procedure (8-10 sentences) using 'each' and 'every' naturally.
writingActivities.hint: Describe a process where some steps are individual (each) and some are for everyone (every).

writingActivities.hint: Fix wrong word choice, missing 'of', or inappropriate contexts.

writingActivities.question: Write formal vs informal alternatives using each/every.
writingActivities.hint: Formal: each/every. Informal: all, each one, every single one.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct determiner for individual focus.
gameActivities.sentence: ____ employee received a bonus. (emphasizing separate bonuses)
gameActivities.hint: Each emphasizes individual treatment of each person.

gameActivities.question: Select the correct word for complete group reference.
gameActivities.sentence: ____ student must submit homework. (all students without exception)
gameActivities.hint: Every refers to the complete group of all students.

gameActivities.question: Which construction requires 'of'?
gameActivities.sentence: ____ the candidates were interviewed. (all individual candidates)
gameActivities.hint: Each of is used before determiners and pronouns.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct word for expressing regularity.
gameActivities.sentence: The bus arrives ____ 30 minutes. (regular complete schedule)
gameActivities.hint: Every is used for regular, repeated complete cycles.

gameActivities.question: Select the more emphatic form.
gameActivities.sentence: ____ one of you is important. (emphasizing every individual)
gameActivities.hint: Each and every is used for emphasis and means the same as every.

quizActivities.question: Which word can be used with just two items?
quizActivities.sentence: He has a tattoo on ____ arm.
quizActivities.hint: Each can be used with two items, but every needs three or more.
quizActivities.explanation: Each can refer to just two arms. Every implies a larger complete set.

quizActivities.question: Which word is used for regularity and frequency?
quizActivities.hint: Every is used for regular, repeated complete cycles.
quizActivities.explanation: Every expresses regularity (every single day). Each would mean separate days.

quizActivities.question: What's the difference between 'each' and 'every'?
quizActivities.sentence: ____ child in the class has a book.
options: Each = individual focus, every = complete group
Each = complete group, every = individual focus
Each is plural, every is singular
quizActivities.correctAnswer: Each = individual focus, every = complete group
quizActivities.hint: Each emphasizes one-by-one treatment, every refers to all members together.
quizActivities.explanation: Each focuses on individual members, every refers to the complete group without exceptions.

quizActivities.question: Which construction is correct?
quizActivities.sentence: The teacher spoke to ____ of the students.
quizActivities.hint: Each of is used before determiners like 'the'.
quizActivities.explanation: Each of the is the correct construction before determiners and pronouns.

quizActivities.question: Which sentence uses the words correctly?
options: Each student in my class is very talented.
Every student in my class is very talented.
quizActivities.hint: Both can be correct depending on whether you emphasize individuals or the complete group.
quizActivities.explanation: Both are grammatically correct. Each emphasizes individual talent, every emphasizes the complete group's talent.
